scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

interpretation_history.interpretation: Route completion for Aug‑Sep 2026 is 0.88 (88%) against a target of 0.95 (95%) with 9,200 manual read accounts, indicating field reads are below target and may lead to estimation substitution.
The dispute ticket volume rose from about 600 in June and July to 1180 in August and 1260 in September, confirming a roughly two‑fold increase since August.
The observation shows disputed bills split by read type: 1,240 linked to ESTIMATED reads and 1,785 to ACTUAL reads, indicating that a majority of disputed bills have actual meter reads.
The tariff change log contains no records, indicating that no tariff changes have been made recently; therefore tariff changes are not a source of the billing errors driving the dispute ticket surge.

E-05.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder reports a shortage of three field readers since July, causing routes to run late and resulting in estimated bills for affected customers.
The dispute response times are within the SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days < 3 days SLA), indicating that response speed is not a driver of the dispute surge.

E-07.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder reports no tariff changes this year, indicating tariff changes are not a source of the billing errors driving the dispute ticket surge.

G-1.statement: dispute volume back to pre-August baseline with correct bills

framing_assertion.rationale: The initial request states that dispute tickets have doubled since August and attributes this to wrong bills.

hypotheses.statement: Inaccurate meter reads (AMI interval or field manual) produce incorrect bills, driving the dispute ticket surge.
hypotheses.rationale: If true, fixing meter‑read quality is required; an AI agent that only answers tickets would treat the symptom.

hypotheses.statement: Recent changes to billing import validation rules introduced systematic billing errors.
hypotheses.rationale: If true, correcting the validation rules eliminates the root cause; an AI agent would only mask the issue.

hypotheses.statement: Delayed or incomplete AMI read exports force estimation substitution, resulting in wrong bills.
hypotheses.rationale: If true, improving the AMI‑to‑MDMS pipeline is needed; an AI agent would still need to address the underlying data gap.

hypotheses.statement: Field dispatch route changes lack the required runtime confirmation, causing missed manual reads and estimation errors.
hypotheses.rationale: If true, enforcing the K‑DISPATCH confirmation step resolves the cause; an AI agent would not fix the process gap.

proposal.root_problem: Low field route completion (< target) caused by staffing shortage leads to increased estimation substitution and/or inaccurate manual reads, which produce incorrect bills and increase dispute tickets.
proposal.requested_solution: Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.
causal_chain: Staffing shortage (3 readers missing since July)
Field route completion falls below target (0.88 vs 0.95)
Increased estimation substitution and/or inaccurate manual reads
Rise in dispute tickets (doubled since Aug)
